title: International Telecommunication Union
definition: The International Telecommunication Union (ITU) is the specialized agency of the United Nations responsible for issues concerning information and communication technologies (ICTs), allocating global radio spectrum and satellite orbits, and developing technical standards.
importanceInUpsc: Frequently tested in UPSC Prelims regarding UN specialized agencies, headquarters, specialized bodies, and India's membership/elections. In Mains GS Paper II and III, it relates to international organizations, global governance of emerging technologies (AI, 5G/6G, cybersecurity), and digital inclusion.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of International Telecommunication Union.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Core foundational concepts of International Organizations and UN specialized agencies
